decisions.reason: The kernel definition permits distinct source and target spaces, while iteration requires an endokernel. Specified P from (X,X-sigma) to itself, D measurable there, and nu on that same space; the positive-time minorization is otherwise unchanged.

F1 incorrectly attributed the finite-partition construction to the measurable-space definition. Built the atoms of the first n specified generators explicitly, verified refinement and product generation, and retained finite-algebra approximation. Occupancy greater than 3/4 in one positive tensor cell gives positive section-threshold sets and overlap at least phi(V)/2. No selection theorem or AC is needed.

The proof uses countable unions over deterministic times and rational thresholds, not measurable selection. Corrected A1 and axiom_use to retain exactly the explicit Choice hypotheses of the canonical path-law and strong Markov suppliers. Checked invariant mass via the positive time-sum, repeated visits via uniform success probability, measurable finite-horizon backward recursions, and the disjoint stationary last-visit contradiction; the claim and its hypotheses remain unchanged.

F2 supplied only measurable kernel evaluations, so it did not justify the parameterized convolution integral. Added the already-declared integration theorem as F4 and specified the lifted probability kernel from (x,y) to z. For each x every candidate density is dominated by P^n and hence at most its absolutely continuous density almost everywhere off the singular support; the finite maximum preserves the residual. The recursive domination gives both pointwise inequalities, and irreducibility on the complement of countably many singular supports gives positivity of the density sum.

F4 wrongly attributed countable generation to the measurable-space definition; it is part of the assumed phi-irreducibility interface. Corrected that attribution and built the countable Boolean generating algebra explicitly. Checked measurability of all minorization sets by finite-measure approximation, additive closure of return-minorization times, the disjoint cyclic family after removal of all points reaching overlaps, and the finite gcd-one argument yielding cofinite times. Clarified that aperiodicity excludes cyclic families without requiring coverage.

The stated argument uses the stronger fact that pi=delta_1 has only one positive-mass state. Any measurable set of positive pi mass contains 1, so two disjoint positive-pi sets cannot exist, even in a cyclic family that does not cover the space. Thus the partition wording does not leave a mathematical gap. Verified one-step accessibility, invariance of delta_1, the telescoping survival probability (x-1)(x+n)/(x(x+n-1)), and its positive limit, which gives both failure of Harris recurrence and the exact TV distance. No edit is needed.

The original nonconvergence sentence omitted the initial law: starting from pi gives pi at every time. Specified either fixed starting state and counting irreducibility measure, and noted that the stationary initial law remains invariant. Matrix powers alternate the two point masses, both at exact TV distance 1/2 from pi, while the two singleton classes form a period-two cyclic family. No item cites this example; its companion-page summary remains a valid description of point-start oscillation.

The absorption argument only forces phi(H-complement)=0 after assuming H is nonempty and fixing a state in H; added that contradiction case. Invariance then gives pi(H-complement)=0, contradicting pi(C)>0. Also handled starts inside C separately by P^m(x,C)>=epsilon nu(C)>0, ensuring the strictly positive witness times required by the cofinite-time supplier for every state. Finite truncation of the petite mixture gives a uniform hitting bound, and padding the remaining times gives one common minorization on D.

F4 only concludes petite and F5 only concludes small, without promising the output minorizer. Replaced both unsupported same-minorizer upgrades by explicit compositions: any probability mu reaches the phi-positive C0 at a common positive time with positive integrated probability, after which the C0 minorization yields nu-prime. Shifted the petite mixture to obtain the common minorizer required by F5; then similarly extended its arbitrary small-set minorizer back into nu-prime. Checked absolute continuity, finite V moments, all-state access for the cofinite-time lemma, bounded C0 drift, and the final skeleton and residual bounds. The full Statement is unchanged.

The fixed-pair coupling lemma does not state that its couplings form a kernel measurable in a random initial second state. Replaced the conditional coupling construction by integration of its uniform fixed-pair event bound against pi, followed by the event supremum; this uses only measurable kernel evaluations and the previously proved finite pi V. Checked the skeleton remainder contraction and the extended-certificate restriction: {V<infinity} is absorbing and full pi, phi ignores its complement, the restricted small-set minorizer has full mass there, and any cyclic family would contradict original aperiodicity. Both stated branches are preserved.

A1 attributed an infinite refresh construction to the axiom itself. Added the already-declared canonical path-law corollary as F8 and supplied the marked probability kernel explicitly. Its cylinder probabilities give geometric holding times, independent Lebesgue refresh states and infinitely many refreshes, so positive-Lebesgue sets are hit almost surely. Checked self-loop exclusion of cyclic families, normalization and invariance of density 1/(2 sqrt(x)), and the positive-pi set where singleton persistence has base greater than any proposed common geometric rate. Choice is retained only for actual path-law and convergence suppliers.

The axiom is a choice-function assumption, not a claim that the geometric theorem interface describes a canonical coupling construction. Restated A1 as the Choice assumption under which F5 is invoked, retaining its actual inherited requirements. Checked the invariant masses by incoming probabilities and detailed balance, counting irreducibility and self-loops, the one-step singleton minorization with epsilon=1, and PV/V=1/4+sqrt(2)/2<24/25 off zero. The bounded boundary drift with b=1 meets every hypothesis of the repaired geometric theorem.
